rows.confidence_limitations: Green/blue beryl is a visible clue, but Be grade needs assay; most beryl is not gem-quality.
rows.name: Beryllium
rows.strategic_importance: Beryllium makes ultra-light stiff alloys for aerospace and precision electronics; it occurs as beryl in pegmatites and greisens.

rows.confidence_limitations: Chromium is confirmed by assay of chromite; the ultramafic host and chromite layers are the geological cue.
rows.name: Chromium
rows.strategic_importance: Chromium is essential to stainless steel and superalloys and is a useful pathfinder for platinum-group metals.

rows.confidence_limitations: Cobalt rarely forms its own ore; look for it with copper or nickel, and confirm by assay.
rows.name: Cobalt
rows.strategic_importance: Cobalt stabilises EV battery cathodes and hardens aerospace superalloys; it rides along with copper in sediment-hosted systems and with nickel in laterites.

rows.confidence_limitations: Green/blue copper staining is a strong indicator; map the alteration zoning and assay to gauge a system.
rows.name: Copper
rows.strategic_importance: Copper is the metal of electrification — wiring, motors, renewables and EVs all depend on it; it forms giant porphyry systems and sediment-hosted belts.

rows.confidence_limitations: Red/blue crystals may be corundum or garnet/spinel; hardness and gemological testing confirm identity and quality.
exploration_indicators: corundum crystals in marble or alkali basalt
rows.name: Ruby & Sapphire
rows.strategic_importance: Ruby and sapphire are gem varieties of corundum (aluminium oxide), second only to diamond in hardness and used in optics and bearings as well as jewellery; they form in marbles and alkali basalts.

rows.confidence_limitations: Not every kimberlite is diamond-bearing — only a small fraction of pipes are economic; the productive next step is to search for indicator minerals (pyrope garnet, chrome diopside) and pipe morphology.
rows.name: Diamond
rows.strategic_importance: Diamond is both the ultimate gemstone and a critical industrial abrasive; nearly all natural diamond is delivered to surface by kimberlite from the deep mantle beneath old cratons.

rows.confidence_limitations: Green colour alone is not emerald; clarity, colour and origin need gemological testing.
exploration_indicators: beryl in mica schist near pegmatite
rows.name: Emerald
rows.strategic_importance: Emerald is green beryl coloured by chromium or vanadium and one of the most valued gems; it forms where beryllium-rich fluids meet chromium-bearing host rocks.

rows.confidence_limitations: Quartz veins and iron staining are encouraging but not proof of gold; the next field step is to look for sulphides (pyrite, arsenopyrite) and to sample fresh vein material for assay.
rows.name: Gold
rows.strategic_importance: Gold is prized for its conductivity and corrosion resistance in electronics and aerospace as well as its use as a store of value; explorers chase it in quartz-vein and shear-hosted systems worldwide.

rows.confidence_limitations: A grey shiny rock may be graphite or molybdenite/sulphide; a streak and flake test plus assay confirm grade.
rows.name: Graphite
rows.strategic_importance: Graphite is the main anode material in lithium-ion batteries and a key refractory; the best flake deposits sit in high-grade metamorphic rocks.

rows.confidence_limitations: Banded iron formation is diagnostic in outcrop; grade depends on hematite/magnetite enrichment, confirmed by assay.
rows.name: Iron
rows.strategic_importance: Iron is the foundation of steel and modern construction; the great deposits are banded iron formations enriched by weathering.

rows.confidence_limitations: Confirming lithium means identifying spodumene/lepidolite and assaying; a plain granite or pegmatite is only a starting point.
rows.name: Lithium
rows.strategic_importance: Lithium is the backbone of electric-vehicle batteries and grid storage; explorers target lithium-rich (LCT) pegmatites and salar brines.

rows.confidence_limitations: Black coatings can be manganese or other oxides; confirm with assay.
rows.name: Manganese
rows.strategic_importance: Manganese is essential to steelmaking and increasingly to battery cathodes; it accumulates in marine sediments and supergene blankets.

rows.confidence_limitations: Nickel in ultramafic rock is common at trace levels; an economic target needs sulphide accumulation or lateritic enrichment, confirmed by assay.
rows.name: Nickel
rows.strategic_importance: Nickel gives stainless steel its strength and is a key cathode metal in EV batteries; it forms in ultramafic magmatic sulphide systems and in tropical laterites over ultramafic rock.

rows.confidence_limitations: Niobium tracks with REE in carbonatites; mineral identification and assay confirm it.
rows.name: Niobium
rows.strategic_importance: Niobium micro-alloys strengthen the steel in pipelines and cars and enables superconductors; carbonatites are its dominant source.

rows.confidence_limitations: PGM grades are invisible in hand specimen and need assay; the geological signal is the mafic-ultramafic host and chromitite layering.
rows.name: Platinum Group Metals
rows.strategic_importance: Platinum, palladium and rhodium are critical catalysts for clean-air technology and hydrogen fuel cells; they concentrate in layered mafic-ultramafic intrusions.

rows.confidence_limitations: REE minerals are often radioactive and fine-grained; a scintillometer reading and mineralogical/assay work are the real confirmation.
rows.name: Rare Earth Elements
rows.strategic_importance: Rare earths power the permanent magnets in wind turbines and EV motors and are strategic for defence and electronics; carbonatites and ion-adsorption clays are the main sources.

rows.confidence_limitations: Silver is usually confirmed by assay of sulphide-bearing veins rather than by eye; look for galena and sphalerite alongside it.
rows.name: Silver
rows.strategic_importance: Silver is the best electrical conductor of all metals and is central to solar panels and electronics; it commonly travels with lead and zinc in epithermal and volcanogenic systems.

rows.confidence_limitations: Columbite-tantalite is dense and dark but needs assay to separate Ta from Nb; the pegmatite context is the first clue.
rows.name: Tantalum
rows.strategic_importance: Tantalum makes the tiny high-performance capacitors in phones and computers and is used in medical and aerospace alloys; it occurs with lithium and tin in evolved pegmatites.

rows.confidence_limitations: Cassiterite is heavy and can be panned, but confirm with assay; a plain granite is not yet a tin deposit.
rows.name: Tin
rows.strategic_importance: Tin is the solder that joins virtually all electronics and coats steel cans; it comes from cassiterite in evolved granites, greisens and downstream placers.

rows.confidence_limitations: Coloured (gem) tourmaline is rare; most is black schorl — a useful exploration indicator rather than a gem in itself.
rows.name: Tourmaline
rows.strategic_importance: Tourmaline is both a gemstone family and a piezoelectric mineral; its presence flags evolved pegmatite/greisen systems that may also carry lithium, tin and tantalum.

rows.confidence_limitations: Scheelite fluoresces blue under UV — a great field test — but grade still needs assay.
rows.name: Tungsten
rows.strategic_importance: Tungsten gives cutting tools and drill bits their hardness and heat resistance; it concentrates in skarns and greisens around granites.

rows.confidence_limitations: Uranium is found with a scintillometer, not the eye; radioactivity plus assay confirm it, and handling needs care.
rows.name: Uranium
rows.strategic_importance: Uranium fuels low-carbon nuclear power and medical isotopes; it concentrates at redox fronts in sandstones and at basement unconformities.

rows.confidence_limitations: Vanadium is locked in magnetite and needs assay; the mafic-intrusion host is the geological cue.
exploration_indicators: titaniferous magnetite layers in mafic rock
rows.name: Vanadium
rows.strategic_importance: Vanadium strengthens steel and powers grid-scale redox-flow batteries; it rides in titaniferous magnetite of layered mafic intrusions.
